FIELD NOTE / 05

Mantra Mādhurya: an evening for the first women-recited Vedic album

Veda Nāda presents S. Aishwarya and S. Saundarya at Jama The Studio, Bengaluru, on Sunday 11 October. The evening marks the launch of the World's First Women Recited Vedic Album.

LOHITESH · 9 OCTOBER 2026
IN THIS STORY
The eveningWhy it matters
BACK TO THE JOURNAL ↗

On Sunday, 11 October, Veda Nāda presents Mantra Mādhurya, a concert by the sisters S. Aishwarya and S. Saundarya. The evening marks the launch of the World's First Women Recited Vedic Album.

The sisters are great-granddaughters of M. S. Subbulakshmi and granddaughters of Radha Viswanathan, a family whose voices have carried Carnatic music and Sanskrit hymns to listeners for generations. In 2017 they sang the benediction Maithreem Bhajatha at the Prime Minister's residence.

The evening

  • When: Sunday, 11 October 2026, 6:30 – 8:30 PM

  • Where: Jama The Studio, 18, 9th Main Road, Jayanagara 2nd Block, Bengaluru 560011

  • Seating: unreserved: first come, first served

  • After the programme: Prasāda, in the measure of dinner

Every ticket directly supports the organisers, performers & the cause

Why it matters

Vedic recitation has long been heard in a small number of voices. An album recited by women, launched on a concert stage in Bengaluru, invites a much wider audience to listen, and Veda Nāda has spent five years building exactly that audience.

Seats are limited and this is a small room. If you plan to come, book early.

Mantra Mādhurya: a houseful evening, and a first for Vedic recitation

On 11 October, S. Aishwarya and S. Saundarya launched the World's First Women Recited Vedic Album at Jama The Studio. Every seat was taken, people stood at the back to the last note, and the night ended with Prasāda served as dinner.
